questions.prompt: Three friends choose a driver by flipping a fair coin twice: HH = Ana, HT = Ben, TH = Cy, and TT = flip twice again. Is this fair?
questions.prompt_markup: Three friends choose a driver by flipping a fair coin twice: HH = Ana, HT = Ben, TH = Cy, and TT = flip twice again. Is this fair?

choices.text: No: TT is ignored, so the three probabilities add to 3/4 instead of 1.
Yes: each friend has probability 1/4, the same as each of the four outcomes.
Yes: HH, HT, and TH are equally likely and TT is redone, so each friend has probability 1/3.
No: Ana has probability 1/2, because HH has two heads and the others have only one.

questions.correct_answer: Yes: HH, HT, and TH are equally likely and TT is redone, so each friend has probability 1/3.
questions.grading_note: Redoing TT scales 1/4 each to 1/3 each.

questions.prompt_markup: A random number generator gives a whole number 1-100, each equally likely. Numbers 1-33 choose A, 34-66 choose B, 67-99 choose C, and 100 means generate again. Is this fair?

choices.text: Yes: each has probability 33/100, and the leftover 1/100 does not matter.
Yes: each person has 33 equally likely numbers, and 100 is redone, so each has 1/3.
No: A has 33 numbers but C has 34 numbers, so C is a little more likely.
